text: a primitive root; to soil, especially in a moral sense:--corrupt, defile, X greatly, pollute, profane.

title: H2611 · chaneph
text:
from 2610; soiled (i.e. with sin), impious:-- hypocrite(-ical). 
 

See  H2610

title: H2612 · choneph
text:
from 2610; moral filth, i.e. wickedness:--hypocrisy. 
 

See  H2610

title: H2613 · chanuphah
text:
feminine from 2610; impiety:--profaneness. 
 

See  H2610

title: H2614 · chanaq
text:
a primitive root (compare 2596); to be narrow; by implication, to throttle, or (reflex.) to choke oneself to death (by a rope):--hang self, strangle. 
 

See  H2596

title: H2615 · Channathon
text:
probably from 2603; favored; Channathon, a place in Palestine:--Hannathon. 
 

See  H2603

title: H2616 · chacad
text:
a primitive root; properly, perhaps to bow (the neck only (compare 2603) in courtesy to an equal), i.e. to be kind; also (by euphem. (compare 1288), but rarely) to reprove:--shew self merciful, put to shame. 
 

See  H2603  
See  H1288

title: H2617 · checed
text:
from 2616; kindness; by implication (towards God) piety: rarely (by opposition) reproof, or (subject.) beauty:--favour, good deed(-liness, -ness), kindly, (loving-)kindness, merciful (kindness), mercy, pity, reproach, wicked thing. 
 

See  H2616

title: H2618 · Checed
text:
the same as 2617: favor; Chesed, an Israelite:--Hesed. 
 

See  H2617

title: H2619 · Chacadyah
text:
from 2617 and 3050; Jah has favored: Chasadjah, an Israelite:--Hasadiah. 
 

See  H2617  
See  H3050

title: H2620 · chacah
text:
a primitive root; to flee for protection (compare 982); figuratively, to confide in:--have hope, make refuge, (put) trust. 
 

See  H982

title: H2621 · Chocah
text:
from 2620; hopeful; Chosah, an Israelite; also a place in Palestine:--Hosah. 
 

See  H2620

title: H2622 · chacuwth
text:
from 2620; confidence:--trust. 
 

See  H2620

title: H2623 · chaciyd
text:
from 2616; properly, kind, i.e. (religiously) pious (a saint):--godly (man), good, holy (one), merciful, saint, (un- )godly. 
 

See  H2616

title: H2624 · chaciydah
text:
feminine of 2623; the kind (maternal) bird, i.e. a stork:--X  feather, stork. 
 

See  H2623

title: H2625 · chaciyl
text:
from 2628; the ravager, i.e. a locust:--caterpillar. 
 

See  H2628

title: H2626 · chaciyn
text:
from 2630; properly, firm, i.e. (by implication) mighty:--strong. 
 

See  H2630

title: H2627 · chacciyr (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) from a root corresponding to 2637; deficient:--wanting. 
 

See  H2637

title: H2628 · chacal
text: a primitive root; to eat off:--consume.

title: H2629 · chacam
text: a primitive root; to muzzle; by analogy, to stop the nose:--muzzle, stop.

title: H2630 · chacan
text: a primitive root; properly, to (be) compact; by implication, to hoard:--lay up.

title: H2631 · chacan (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 2630; to hold in occupancy:--possess. 
 

See  H2630

title: H2632 · checen (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) from 2631; strength:--power. 
 

See  H2631

title: H2633 · chocen
text:
from 2630; wealth:--riches, strength, treasure. 
 

See  H2630

title: H2634 · chacon
text:
from 2630; powerful:--strong. 
 

See  H2630

title: H2635 · chacaph (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of 2636; a clod:--clay. 
 

See  H2636

title: H2636 · chacpac
text: reduplicated from an unused root meaning apparently to peel; a shred or scale:--round thing.

title: H2637 · chacer
text: a primitive root; to lack; by implication, to fail, want, lessen:--be abated, bereave, decrease, (cause to) fail, (have) lack, make lower, want.

title: H2638 · chacer
text:
from 2637; lacking; hence, without:--destitute, fail, lack, have need, void, want. 
 

See  H2637

title: H2639 · checer
text:
from 2637; lack; hence, destitution:--poverty, want. 
 

See  H2637

title: H2640 · chocer
text:
from 2637; poverty:--in want of. 
 

See  H2637

title: H2641 · Chacrah
text:
from 2637; want:--Chasrah, an Israelite:--Hasrah. 
 

See  H2637

title: H2642 · checrown
text:
from 2637; deficiency:--wanting. 
 

See  H2637

title: H2643 · chaph
text:
from 2653 (in the moral sense of covered from soil); pure:--innocent. 
 

See  H2653

title: H2644 · chapha'
text:
an orthographical variation of 2645; properly, to cover, i.e. (in a sinister sense) to act covertly:--do secretly. 
 

See  H2645

title: H2645 · chaphah
text:
a primitive root (compare 2644, 2653); to cover; by implication, to veil, to encase, protect:--ceil, cover, overlay. 
 

See  H2644  
See  H2653

title: H2646 · chuppah
text:
from 2645; a canopy:--chamber, closet, defence. 
 

See  H2645

title: H2647 · Chuppah
text:
the same as 2646; Chuppah, an Israelite:--Huppah. 
 

See  H2646

title: H2648 · chaphaz
text: a primitive root; properly, to start up suddenly, i.e. (by implication) to hasten away, to fear:--(make) haste (away), tremble.

title: H2649 · chippazown
text:
from 2468; hasty flight:--haste. 
 

See  H2468

title: H2650 · Chuppiym
text:
plural of 2646 (compare 2349); Chuppim, an Israelite:--Huppim. 
 

See  H2646  
See  H2349

title: H2651 · chophen
text: from an unused root of uncertain signification; a fist (only in the dual):--fists, (both) hands, hand(-ful).

title: H2652 · Chophniy
text:
from 2651; perhaps pugilist; Chophni, an Israelite:--Hophni. 
 

See  H2651

title: H2653 · chophaph
text:
a primitive root (compare 2645, 3182); to cover (in protection):--cover. 
 

See  H2645  
See  H3182

title: H2654 · chaphets
text: a primitive root; properly, to incline to; by implication (literally but rarely) to bend; figuratively, to be pleased with, desire:--X any at all, (have, take) delight, desire, favour, like, move, be (well) pleased, have pleasure, will, would.

title: H2655 · chaphets
text:
from 2654; pleased with:--delight in, desire, favour, please, have pleasure, whosoever would, willing, wish. 
 

See  H2654

title: H2656 · chephets
text:
from 2654; pleasure; hence (abstractly) desire; concretely, a valuable thing; hence (by extension) a matter (as something in mind):--acceptable, delight(-some), desire, things desired, matter, pleasant(-ure), purpose, willingly. 
 

See  H2654

title: H2657 · Chephtsiy bahh
text:
from 2656 with suffixes; my delight (is) in her; Cheptsi-bah, a fanciful name for Palestine:--Hephzi-bah. 
 

See  H2656

title: H2658 · chaphar
text: a primitive root; properly, to pry into; by implication, to delve, to explore:--dig, paw, search out, seek.

title: H2659 · chapher
text:
a primitive root (perhaps rath. the same as 2658 through the idea of detection): to blush; figuratively, to be ashamed, disappointed; causatively, to shame, reproach:--be ashamed, be confounded, be brought to confusion (unto shame), come (be put to) shame, bring reproach. 
 

See  H2658

title: H2660 · Chepher
text:
from 2658 or 2659; a pit of shame; Chepher, a place in Palestine; also the name of three Israelites:--Hepher. 
 

See  H2658  
See  H2659

title: H2661 · chaphor
text:
from 2658; a hole; only in connection with 6512, which ought rather to be joined as one word, thus chapharperah {khaf-ar- pay-raw'}; by reduplication from 2658; a burrower, i.e. probably a rat:--+ mole. 
 

See  H2658  
See  H6512  
See  H2658

title: H2662 · Chephriy
text:
patronymically from 2660; a Chephrite (collectively) or descendants of Chepher:--Hepherites. 
 

See  H2660

title: H2663 · Chapharayim
text:
dual of 2660; double pit; Chapharajim, a place in Palestine:--Haphraim. 
 

See  H2660

title: H2664 · chaphas
text: a primitive root; to seek; causatively, to conceal oneself (i.e. let be sought), or mask:--change, (make) diligent (search), disquise self, hide, search (for, out).

title: H2665 · chephes
text:
from 2664; something covert, i.e. a trick:--search. 
 

See  H2664

title: H2666 · chaphash
text: a primitive root; to spread loose; figuratively, to manumit:--be free.

title: H2667 · Chophesh
text:
from 2666; something spread loosely, i.e. a carpet:--precious. 
 

See  H2666

title: H2668 · chuphshah
text:
from 2666; liberty (from slavery):--freedom. 
 

See  H2666

title: H2669 · chophshuwth
text:
and chophshiyth {khof-sheeth'}; from 2666; prostration by sickness (with 1004, a hospital):--several. 
 

See  H2666  
See  H1004

title: H2670 · chophshiy
text:
from 2666; exempt (from bondage, tax or care):--free, liberty. 
 

See  H2666

title: H2671 · chets
text:
from 2686; properly, a piercer, i.e. an arrow; by implication, a wound; figuratively, (of God) thunder-bolt; (by interchange for 6086) the shaft of a spear:--+ archer, arrow, dart, shaft, staff, wound. 
 

See  H2686  
See  H6086

title: H2672 · chatsab
text: or chatseb {khaw-tsabe'}; a primitive root ; to cut or carve (wood), stone or other material); by implication, to hew, split, square, quarry, engrave:--cut, dig, divide, grave, hew (out, -er), made, mason.

title: H2673 · chatsah
text:
a primitive root (compare 2086)); to cut or split in two; to halve:--divide, X live out half, reach to the midst, participle 
 

See  H2086

title: H2674 · Chatsowr
text:
a collective form of 2691; village; Chatsor, the name (thus simply) of two places in Palestine and of one in Arabia:-- Hazor. 
 

See  H2691

title: H2675 · Chatsowr Chadattah
text:
from 2674 and a Aramaizing form of the feminine of 2319 (compare 2323); new Chatsor, a place in Palestine:--Hazor, Hadattah (as if two places). 
 

See  H2674  
See  H2323

title: H2676 · chatsowth
text:
from 2673; the middle (of the night):--mid(-night). 
 

See  H2673

title: H2677 · chetsiy
text:
from 2673; the half or middle:--half, middle, mid(-night), midst, part, two parts. 
 

See  H2673

title: H2678 · chitstsiy
text:
or chetsiy {chay-tsee'}; prolongation from 2671; an arrow:--arrow. 
 

See  H2671

title: H2679 · Chatsiy ham-M@nuchowth
text:
from 2677 and the plural of 4496, with the article interposed; midst of the resting- places; Chatsi-ham-Menuchoth, an Israelite:--half of the Manahethites. 
 

See  H2677  
See  H4496

title: H2680 · Chatsiy ham-M@nachti
text:
patronymically from 2679; a Chatsi-ham-Menachtite or descendant of Chatsi-ham-Menuchoth:--half of the Manahethites. 
 

See  H2679

title: H2681 · chatsiyr
text:
a collateral form of 2691; a court or abode:--court. 
 

See  H2691

title: H2682 · chatsiyr
text:
perhaps originally the same as 2681, from the greenness of a courtyard; grass; also a leek (collectively):--grass, hay, herb, leek. 
 

See  H2681

title: H2683 · chetsen
text: from an unused root meaning to hold firmly; the bosom (as comprised between the arms):--bosom.

title: H2684 · chotsen
text:
a collateral form of 2683, and meaning the same:--arm, lap. 
 

See  H2683

title: H2685 · chatsaph (Aramaic)
text: (Aramaic) a primitive root; properly, to shear or cut close; figuratively, to be severe:--hasty, be urgent.

title: H2686 · chatsats
text:
a primitive root (compare 2673); properly, to chop into, pierce or sever; hence, to curtail, to distribute (into ranks); as denom. from 2671, to shoot an arrow:--archer, X  bands, cut off in the midst. 
 

See  H2673  
See  H2671

title: H2687 · chatsats
text:
from 2687; properly, something cutting; hence, gravel (as grit); also (like 2671) an arrow:--arrow, gravel (stone). 
 

See  H2687  
See  H2671

title: H2688 · Chats@tsown Tamar
text:
or Chatsatson Tamar {khats-ats-one' taw-mawr'}; from 2686 and 8558; division (i.e. perhaps row) of (the) palm-tree; Chatsetson-tamar, a place in Palestine:--Hazezon- tamar. 
 

See  H2686  
See  H8558

title: H2689 · chatsots@rah
text:
by reduplication from 2690; a trumpet (from its sundered or quavering note):--trumpet(-er). 
 

See  H2690

title: H2690 · chatsar
text:
a primitive root; properly, to surround with a stockade, and thus separate from the open country; but used only in the reduplicated form chatsotser {khast-o-tsare'}; or (2 Chronicles 5:12) chatsorer {khats-o-rare'}; as dem. from 2689; to trumpet, i.e. blow on that instrument:--blow, sound, trumpeter. 
 

See  H2689

title: H2691 · chatser
text:
(masculine and feminine); from 2690 in its original sense; a yard (as inclosed by a fence); also a hamlet (as similarly surrounded with walls):--court, tower, village. 
 

See  H2690

title: H2692 · Chatsar Addar
text:
from 2691 and 146; (the) village of Addar; Chatsar-Addar, a place in Palestine:--Hazar-addar. 
 

See  H2691  
See  H146

title: H2693 · Chatsar Gaddah
text:
from 2691 and a feminine of 1408; (the) village of (female) Fortune; Chatsar-Gaddah, a place in Palestine:--Hazar-gaddah. 
 

See  H2691  
See  H1408

title: H2694 · Chatsar hat-Tiykown
text:
from 2691 and 8484 with the article interposed; village of the middle; Chatsar-hat-Tikon, a place in Palestine:--Hazar-hatticon. 
 

See  H2691  
See  H8484

title: H2695 · Chetsrow
text:
by an orthographical variation for 2696; enclosure; Chetsro, an Israelite:--Hezro, Hezrai. 
 

See  H2696

title: H2696 · Chetsrown
text:
from 2691; court-yard; Chetsron, the name of a place in Palestine; also of two Israelites:--Hezron. 
 

See  H2691

title: H2697 · Chetsrowniy
text:
patronymically from 2696; a Chetsronite or (collectively) descendants of Chetsron:--Hezronites. 
 

See  H2696

title: H2698 · Chatserowth
text:
feminine plural of 2691; yards; Chatseroth, a place in Palestine:--Hazeroth. 
 

See  H2691

title: H2699 · Chatseriym
text:
plural masculine of 2691; yards; Chatserim, a place in Palestine:--Hazerim. 
 

See  H2691

title: H2700 · Chatsarmaveth
text:
from 2691 and 4194; village of death; Chatsarmaveth, a place in Arabia:--Hazarmaveth. 
 

See  H2691  
See  H4194

title: H2701 · Chatsar Cuwcah
text:
from 2691 and 5484; village of cavalry; Chatsar-Susah, a place in Palestine:--Hazar-susah. 
 

See  H2691  
See  H5484

title: H2702 · Chatsar Cuwciym
text:
from 2691 and the plural of 5483; village of horses; Chatsar-Susim, a place in Palestine:--Hazar- susim. 
 

See  H2691  
See  H5483

title: H2703 · Chatsar `Eynown
text:
from 2691 and a derivative of 5869; village of springs; Chatsar-Enon, a place in Palestine:--Hazar- enon. 
 

See  H2691  
See  H5869

title: H2704 · Chatsar `Eynan
text:
from 2691 and the same as 5881; village of springs; Chatsar-Enan, a place in Palestine:--Hazar-enan. 
 

See  H2691  
See  H5881

title: H2705 · Chatsar Shuw`al
text:
from 2691 and 7776; village of (the) fox; Chatsar-Shual, a place in Palestine:--Hazar-shual. 
 

See  H2691  
See  H7776

title: H2706 · choq
text:
from 2710; an enactment; hence, an appointment (of time, space, quantity, labor or usage):--appointed, bound, commandment, convenient, custom, decree(-d), due, law, measure, X necessary, ordinance(- nary), portion, set time, statute, task. 
 

See  H2710

title: H2707 · chaqah
text: a primitive root; to carve; by implication, to delineate; also to entrench:--carved work, portrayed, set a print.

title: H2708 · chuqqah
text:
feminine of 2706, and meaning substantially the same:--appointed, custom, manner, ordinance, site, statute. 
 

See  H2706

title: H2709 · Chaquwpha'
text: from an unused root probably meaning to bend; crooked; Chakupha, one of the Nethinim:--Hakupha.

title: H2710 · chaqaq
text: a primitive root; properly, to hack, i.e. engrave (Judges 5:14, to be a scribe simply); by implication, to enact (laws being cut in stone or metal tablets in primitive times) or (gen.) prescribe:--appoint, decree, governor, grave, lawgiver, note, pourtray, print, set.

title: H2711 · cheqeq
text:
from 2710; an enactment, a resolution:--decree, thought. 
 

See  H2710

title: H2712 · Chuqqog
text:
or (fully) Chuwqoq {khoo-koke'}; from 2710; appointed; Chukkok or Chukok, a place in Palestine:--Hukkok, Hukok. 
 

See  H2710

title: H2713 · chaqar
text: a primitive root; properly, to penetrate; hence, to examine intimately:--find out, (make) search (out), seek (out), sound, try.

title: H2714 · cheqer
text:
from 2713; examination, enumeration, deliberation:--finding out, number, (un-)search(-able, -ed, out, -ing). 
 

See  H2713

title: H2715 · chor
text:
or (fully) chowr {khore}; from 2787; properly, white or pure (from the cleansing or shining power of fire (compare 2751); hence (figuratively) noble (in rank):--noble. 
 

See  H2787  
See  H2751

title: H2716 · chere'
text: from an unused (and vulgar) root probably meaning to evacuate the bowels: excrement; -dung. Also chariy {khar-ee'}.

title: H2717 · charab
text: or chareb {khaw-rabe'}; a primitive root; to parch (through drought) i.e. (by analogy,) to desolate, destroy, kill:-- decay, (be) desolate, destroy(-er), (be) dry (up), slay, X  surely, (lay, lie, make) waste.

title: H2718 · charab (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) a root corresponding to 2717; to demolish:--destroy. 
 

See  H2717

title: H2719 · chereb
text:
from 2717; drought; also a cutting instrument (from its destructive effect), as a knife, sword, or other sharp implement:--axe, dagger, knife, mattock, sword, tool. 
 

See  H2717

title: H2720 · chareb
text:
from 2717; parched or ruined:--desolate, dry, waste. 
 

See  H2717

title: H2721 · choreb
text:
a collaterally form of 2719; drought or desolation:--desolation, drought, dry, heat, X utterly, waste. 
 

See  H2719

title: H2722 · Choreb
text:
from 2717; desolate; Choreb, a (generic) name for the Sinaitic mountains:--Horeb. 
 

See  H2717

title: H2723 · chorbah
text:
feminine of 2721; properly, drought, i.e. (by implication) a desolation:--decayed place, desolate (place, -tion), destruction, (laid) waste (place). 
 

See  H2721

title: H2724 · charabah
text:
feminine of 2720; a desert:--dry (ground, land). 
 

See  H2720

title: H2725 · charabown
text:
from 2717; parching heat:--drought. 
 

See  H2717

title: H2726 · Charbowna'
text: or Charbownah {khar-bo-naw'}; of Persian origin; Charbona or Charbonah, a eunuch of Xerxes:--Harbona, Harbonah.

title: H2727 · charag
text: a primitive root; properly, to leap suddenly, i.e. (by implication) to be dismayed:--be afraid.

title: H2728 · chargol
text:
from 2727; the leaping insect, i.e. a locust:--beetle. 
 

See  H2727

title: H2729 · charad
text: a primitive root; to shudder with terror; hence, to fear; also to hasten (with anxiety):--be (make) afraid, be careful, discomfit, fray (away), quake, tremble.

title: H2730 · chared
text:
from 2729; fearful; also reverential:--afraid, trembling. 
 

See  H2729

title: H2731 · charadah
text:
feminine of 2730; fear, anxiety:--care, X exceedingly, fear, quaking, trembling. 
 

See  H2730

title: H2732 · Charadah
text:
the same as 2731; Charadah, a place in the Desert:--Haradah. 
 

See  H2731

title: H2733 · Charodiy
text:
patrial from a derivative of 2729 (compare 5878); a Charodite, or inhabitant of Charod:--Harodite. 
 

See  H2729  
See  H5878

title: H2734 · charah
text:
a primitive root (compare 2787); to glow or grow warm; figuratively (usually) to blaze up, of anger, zeal, jealousy:--be angry, burn, be displeased, X earnestly, fret self, grieve, be (wax) hot, be incensed, kindle, X very, be wroth. See 8474. 
 

See  H2787  
See  H8474

title: H2735 · Chor hag-Gidgad
text:
from 2356 and a collateral (masculine) form of 1412, with the article interposed; hole of the cleft: Chor-hag-Gidgad, a place in the Desert:--Hor-hagidgad. 
 

See  H2356  
See  H1412

title: H2736 · Charhayah
text:
; from 2734 and 3050; fearing Jah; Charhajah, an Israelite:--Harhaiah. 
 

See  H2734  
See  H3050

title: H2737 · charuwz
text: from an unused root meaning to perforate; properly, pierced, i.e. a bead of pearl, gems or jewels (as strung):--chain.

title: H2738 · charuwl
text: or (shortened) charul {khaw-rool'}; apparently, a passive participle of an unused root probably meaning to be prickly; properly, pointed, i.e. a bramble or other thorny weed: nettle.

title: H2739 · charuwmaph
text:
from passive participle of 2763 and 639; snub-nosed; Charumaph, an Israelite:--Harumaph. 
 

See  H2763  
See  H639

title: H2740 · charown
text:
or (shortened) charon {khaw-rone'}; from 2734; a burning of anger:--sore displeasure, fierce(-ness), fury, (fierce) wrath(-ful). 
 

See  H2734

title: H2741 · Charuwphiy
text:
a patrial from (probably) a collateral form of 2756; a Charuphite or inhabitant of Charuph (or Chariph):--Haruphite. 
 

See  H2756

title: H2742 · charuwts
text:
or charuts {khaw-roots'}; passive participle of 2782; properly, incised or (active) incisive; hence (as noun masculine or feminine) a trench (as dug), gold (as mined), a threshing-sledge (having sharp teeth); (figuratively) determination; also eager:--decision, diligent, (fine) gold, pointed things, sharp, threshing instrument, wall. 
 

See  H2782

title: H2743 · Charuwts
text:
the same as 2742; earnest; Charuts, an Israelite:--Haruz. 
 

See  H2742

title: H2744 · Charchuwr
text:
a fuller form of 2746; inflammation; Charchur, one of the Nethinim:--Harhur. 
 

See  H2746

title: H2745 · Charchac
text:
from the same as 2775; perhaps shining; Charchas, an Israelite:--Harhas. 
 

See  H2775

title: H2746 · charchur
text:
from 2787; fever (as hot); -extreme burning. 
 

See  H2787

title: H2747 · cheret
text: from a primitive root meaning to engrave; a chisel or graver; also a style for writing:--graving tool, pen.

title: H2748 · chartom
text:
from the same as 2747; a horoscopist (as drawing magical lines or circles):--magician. 
 

See  H2747

title: H2749 · chartom (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) the same as 2748:--magician. 
 

See  H2748

title: H2750 · choriy
text:
from 2734; a burning (i.e. intense) anger:--fierce, X great, heat. 
 

See  H2734

title: H2751 · choriy
text:
from the same as 2353; white bread:--white. 
 

See  H2353

title: H2752 · Choriy
text:
from 2356; cave-dweller or troglodyte; a Chorite or aboriginal Idumaean:--Horims, Horites. 
 

See  H2356

title: H2753 · Choriy
text:
or Chowriy {kho-ree'}; the same as 2752; Chori, the name of two men:--Hori. 
 

See  H2752

title: H2754 · chariyt

from 3787; literally, a director, i.e. the spindle or shank of a distaff (6418), by which it is twirled:--spindle. 
 

See  H3787  
See  H6418

title: H3602 · kakah
text:
from 3541; just so, referring to the previous or following context:--after that (this) manner, this matter, (even) so, in such a case, thus. 
 

See  H3541

title: H3603 · kikkar
text:
from 3769; a circle, i.e. (by implication) a circumjacent tract or region, expec. the Ghor or valley of the Jordan; also a (round) loaf; also a talent (or large (round) coin):--loaf, morsel, piece, plain, talent. 
 

See  H3769

title: H3604 · kikker (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 3603; a talent:--talent. 
 

See  H3603

title: H3605 · kol
text:
or (Jer. 33:8) kowl {kole}; from 3634; properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense):--(in) all (manner, (ye)), altogether, any (manner), enough, every (one, place, thing), howsoever, as many as, (no-)thing, ought, whatsoever, (the) whole, whoso(-ever). 
 

See  H3634

title: H3606 · kol (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 3605:--all, any, + (forasmuch) as, + be-(for this) cause, every, + no (manner, -ne), + there (where)-fore, + though, what (where, who)-soever, (the) whole. 
 

See  H3605

title: H3607 · kala'
text: a primitive root; to restrict, by act (hold back or in) or word (prohibit):--finish, forbid, keep (back), refrain, restrain, retain, shut up, be stayed, withhold.

title: H3608 · kele'
text:
from 3607; a prison:--prison. Compare 3610, 3628. 
 

See  H3607  
See  H3610  
See  H3628

title: H3609 · Kil'ab
text:
apparently from 3607 and 1; restraint of (his) father; Kilab, an Israelite:--Chileab. 
 

See  H3607  
See  H1

title: H3610 · kil'ayim
text:
dual of 3608 in the original sense of separation; two heterogeneities:--divers seeds (-e kinds), mingled (seed). 
 

See  H3608

title: H3611 · keleb
text: from an unused root means. to yelp, or else to attack; a dog; hence (by euphemism) a male prostitute:--dog.

title: H3612 · Kaleb
text:
perhaps a form of 3611, or else from the same root in the sense of forcible; Caleb, the name of three Israelites:--Caleb. 
 

See  H3611

title: H3613 · Kaleb 'Ephrathah
text:
from 3612 and 672; Caleb- Ephrathah, a place in Egypt (if the text is correct):--Caleb-ephrathah. 
 

See  H3612  
See  H672

title: H3614 · Kalibbow
text:
probably by erroneous transcription for Kalebiy {kaw-lay-bee'}; patronymically from 3612; a Calebite or descendant of Caleb:--of the house of Caleb. 
 

See  H3612

title: H3615 · kalah
text: a primitive root; to end, whether intransitive (to cease, be finished, perish) or transitived (to complete, prepare, consume):--accomplish, cease, consume (away), determine, destroy (utterly), be (when ... were) done, (be an) end (of), expire, (cause to) fail, faint, finish, fulfil, X fully, X  have, leave (off), long, bring to pass, wholly reap, make clean riddance, spend, quite take away, waste.

title: H3616 · kaleh
text:
from 3615; pining:--fail. 
 

See  H3615

title: H3617 · kalah
text:
from 3615; a completion; adverb, completely; also destruction:--altogether, (be, utterly) consume(-d), consummation(-ption), was determined, (full, utter) end, riddance. 
 

See  H3615

title: H3618 · kallah
text:
from 3634; a bride (as if perfect); hence, a son's wife:--bride, daughter-in-law, spouse. 
 

See  H3634

title: H3619 · k@lub
text:
from the same as 3611; a bird-trap (as furnished with a clap-stick or treadle to spring it); hence, a basket (as resembling a wicker cage):--basket, cage. 
 

See  H3611

title: H3620 · K@luwb
text:
the same as 3619; Kelub, the name of two Israelites:--Chelub. 
 

See  H3619

title: H3621 · K@luwbay
text:
a form of 3612; Kelubai, an Israelite:  -Chelubai. 
 

See  H3612

title: H3622 · K@luwhay
text:
from 3615; completed; Keluhai, an Israelite:--Chelluh. 
 

See  H3615

title: H3623 · k@luwlah
text:
denominative passive participle from 3618; bridehood (only in the plural):--espousal. 
 

See  H3618

title: H3624 · kelach
text: from an unused root meaning to be complete; maturity:--full (old) age.

title: H3625 · Kelach
text:
the same as 3624; Kelach, a place in Assyria:  -Calah. 
 

See  H3624

title: H3626 · Kol-Chozeh
text:
from 3605 and 2374; every seer; Col- Chozeh, an Israelite:--Col-hozeh. 
 

See  H3605  
See  H2374

title: H3627 · k@liy
text:
from 3615; something prepared, i.e. any apparatus (as an implement, utensil, dress, vessel or weapon):--armour ((-bearer)), artillery, bag, carriage, + furnish, furniture, instrument, jewel, that is made of, X one from another, that which pertaineth, pot, + psaltery, sack, stuff, thing, tool, vessel, ware, weapon, + whatsoever. 
 

See  H3615

title: H3628 · k@liy'
text:
or {kel-oo'}; from 3607 (compare 3608);  a prison:--prison. 
 

See  H3607  
See  H3608

title: H3629 · kilyah
text:
feminine of 3627 (only in the plural); a kidney (as an essential organ); figuratively, the mind (as the interior self):--kidneys, reins. 
 

See  H3627

title: H3630 · Kilyown
text:
a form of 3631; Kiljon, an Israelite:--Chilion. 
 

See  H3631

title: H3631 · killayown
text:
from 3615; pining, destruction:  -consumption, failing. 
 

See  H3615

title: H3632 · kaliyl
text:
from 3634; complete; as noun, the whole (specifically, a sacrifice entirely consumed); as adverb, fully:--all, every whit, flame, perfect(-ion), utterly, whole burnt offering (sacrifice), wholly. 
 

See  H3634

title: H3633 · Kalkol
text:
from 3557; sustenance; Calcol, an Israelite:--Calcol, Chalcol. 
 

See  H3557

title: H3634 · kalal
text: a primitive root; to complete:--(make) perfect.

title: H3635 · k@lal (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 3634; to complete:--finish, make (set) up. 
 

See  H3634

title: H3636 · K@lal
text:
from 3634; complete; Kelal, an Israelite:--Chelal. 
 

See  H3634

title: H3637 · kalam
text: a primitive root; properly, to wound; but only figuratively, to taunt or insult:--be (make) ashamed, blush, be confounded, be put to confusion, hurt, reproach, (do, put to) shame.

title: H3638 · Kilmad
text: of foreign derivation; Kilmad, a place apparently in the Assyrian empire:--Chilmad.

title: H3639 · k@limmah
text:
from 3637; disgrace:--confusion, dishonour, reproach, shame. 
 

See  H3637

title: H3640 · k@limmuwth
text:
from 3639; disgrace:--shame. 
 

See  H3639

title: H3641 · Kalneh
text:
or Kalneh {kal-nay'}; also Kalnow {kal-no'}; of foreign derivation; Calneh or Calno, a place in the Assyrian empire:-- Calneh, Calno. Compare 3656. 
 

See  H3656

title: H3642 · kamahh
text: a primitive root; to pine after:--long.

title: H3643 · Kimham
text:
from 3642; pining; Kimham, an Israelite:--Chimham. 
 

See  H3642

title: H3644 · k@mow
text:
or kamow {kaw-mo'}; a form of the prefix "k-", but used separately (compare 3651); as, thus, so:--according to, (such) as (it were, well as), in comparison of, like (as, to, unto), thus, when, worth. 
 

See  H3651

title: H3645 · K@mowsh
text: or (Jer. 48:7) Kmiysh {kem-eesh'}; from an unused root meaning to subdue; the powerful; Kemosh, the god of the Moabites:--Chemosh.

title: H3646 · kammon
text: from an unused root meaning to store up or preserve; "cummin" (from its use as a condiment):--cummin.

title: H3647 · kamac
text: a primitive root; to store away, i.e. (figuratively) in the memory:--lay up in store.

title: H3648 · kamar
text: a primitive root; properly, to intertwine or contract, i.e. (by implication) to shrivel (as with heat); figuratively, to be deeply affected with passion (love or pity):--be black, be kindled, yearn.

title: H3649 · kamar
text:
from 3648; properly, an ascetic (as if shrunk with self-maceration), i.e. an idolatrous priest (only in plural):--Chemarims (idolatrous) priests. 
 

See  H3648

title: H3650 · kimriyr
text:
redupl. from 3648; obscuration (as if from shrinkage of light, i.e. an eclipse (only in plural):--blackness. 
 

See  H3648

title: H3651 · ken
text:
from 3559; properly, set upright; hence (figuratively as adjective) just; but usually (as adverb or conjunction) rightly or so (in various applications to manner, time and relation; often with other particles):--+ after that (this, -ward, -wards), as ... as, + (for-)asmuch as yet, + be (for which) cause, + following, howbeit, in (the) like (manner, -wise), X the more, right, (even) so, state, straightway, such (thing), surely, + there (where)-fore, this, thus, true, well, X you. 
 

See  H3559

title: H3652 · ken (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 3651; so:--thus. 
 

See  H3651

title: H3653 · ken
text:
the same as 3651, used as a noun; a stand, i.e. pedestal or station:--base, estate, foot, office, place, well. 
 

See  H3651

title: H3654 · ken
text:
from 3661 in the sense of fastening; a gnat (from infixing its sting; used only in plural (and irreg. in Exod. 8:17,18; Heb. 13:14)):--lice, X manner. 
 

See  H3661  
See  H18

title: H3655 · kanah
text: a primitive root; to address by an additional name; hence, to eulogize:--give flattering titles, surname (himself).

title: H3656 · Kanneh
text:
for 3641; Canneh, a place in Assyria:--Canneh. 
 

See  H3641

title: H3657 · kannah
text:
from 3661; a plant (as set):--X vineyard. 
 

See  H3661

title: H3658 · kinnowr
text: from a unused root meaning to twang; a harp:  -harp.

title: H3659 · Konyahuw
text:
for 3204; Conjah, an Israelite king:--Coniah. 
 

See  H3204

title: H3660 · k@nema' (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 3644; so or thus:--so, (in) this manner (sort), thus. 
 

See  H3644

title: H3661 · kanan
text: a primitive root; to set out, i.e. plant:--X vineyard.

title: H3662 · K@naniy
text:
from 3661; planted; Kenani, an Israelite:  -Chenani. 
 

See  H3661

title: H3663 · K@nanyah
text:
or Knanyahuw {ken-an-yaw'-hoo}; from 3661 and 3050; Jah has planted; Kenanjah, an Israelite:--Chenaniah. 
 

See  H3661  
See  H3050

title: H3664 · kanac
text: a primitive root; to collect; hence, to enfold:  -gather (together), heap up, wrap self.

title: H3665 · kana`
text: a primitive root; properly, to bend the knee; hence, to humiliate, vanquish:--bring down (low), into subjection, under, humble (self), subdue.

title: H3666 · kin`ah
text:
from 3665 in the sense of folding (compare 3664); a package:--wares. 
 

See  H3665  
See  H3664

title: H3667 · K@na`an
text:
from 3665; humiliated; Kenaan, a son a Ham; also the country inhabited by him:--Canaan, merchant, traffick. 
 

See  H3665

title: H3668 · K@na`anah
text:
feminine of 3667; Kenaanah, the name of two Israelites:--Chenaanah. 
 

See  H3667

title: H3669 · K@na`aniy
text:
patrial from 3667; a Kenaanite or inhabitant of Kenaan; by implication, a pedlar (the Canaanites standing for their neighbors the Ishmaelites, who conducted mercantile caravans):--Canaanite, merchant, trafficker. 
 

See  H3667

title: H3670 · kanaph
text: a primitive root; properly, to project laterally, i.e. probably (reflexive) to withdraw:--be removed.

title: H3671 · kanaph
text:
from 3670; an edge or extremity; specifically (of a bird or army) a wing, (of a garment or bed-clothing) a flap, (of the earth) a quarter, (of a building) a pinnacle:--+ bird, border, corner, end, feather(-ed), X flying, + (one an-)other, overspreading, X quarters, skirt, X sort, uttermost part, wing((-ed)). 
 

See  H3670

title: H3672 · Kinn@rowth
text:
or Kinnereth {kin-neh'-reth}; respectively plural and singular feminine from the same as 3658; perhaps harp-shaped; Kinneroth or Kinnereth, a place in Palestine:--Chinnereth, Chinneroth, Cinneroth. 
 

See  H3658

title: H3673 · kanash (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 3664; to assemble:--gather together. 
 

See  H3664

title: H3674 · k@nath
text:
from 3655; a colleague (as having the same title):--companion. 
 

See  H3655

title: H3675 · k@nath (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 3674:--companion. 
 

See  H3674

title: H3676 · kec
text:
apparently a contraction for 3678, but probably by erroneous transcription for 5251:--sworn. 
 

See  H3678  
See  H5251

title: H3677 · kece'
text:
or keceh {keh'-seh}; apparently from 3680; properly, fulness or the full moon, i.e. its festival:--(time) appointed. 
 

See  H3680

title: H3678 · kicce'
text:
or kicceh {kis-say'}; from 3680; properly, covered, i.e. a throne (as canopied):--seat, stool, throne. 
 

See  H3680

title: H3679 · Kacday
text:
for 3778:--Chaldean. 
 

See  H3778

title: H3680 · kacah
text:
a primitive root; properly, to plump, i.e. fill up hollows; by implication, to cover (for clothing or secrecy):--clad self, close, clothe, conceal, cover (self), (flee to) hide, overwhelm. Compare 3780. 
 

See  H3780

title: H3681 · kacuwy
text:
passive participle of 3680; properly, covered, i.e. (as noun) a covering:--covering. 
 

See  H3680

title: H3682 · k@cuwth
text:
from 3680; a cover (garment); figuratively, a veiling:--covering, raiment, vesture. 
 

See  H3680

title: H3683 · kacach
text: a primitive root; to cut off:--cut down (up).

title: H3684 · k@ciyl
text:
from 3688;  properly, fat, i.e. (figuratively) stupid or silly:--fool(-ish). 
 

See  H3688

title: H3685 · K@ciyl
text:
the same as 3684; any notable constellation; specifically Orion (as if a burly one):--constellation, Orion. 
 

See  H3684

title: H3686 · K@ciyl
text:
the same as 3684; Kesil, a place in Palestine:  -Chesil. 
 

See  H3684

title: H3687 · k@ciyluwth
text:
from 3684; silliness:--foolish. 
 

See  H3684

title: H3688 · kacal
text: a primitive root; properly, to be fat, i.e. (figuratively) silly:--be foolish.

title: H3689 · kecel
text:
from 3688; properly, fatness, i.e. by implication (literally) the loin (as the seat of the leaf fat) or (generally) the viscera; also (figuratively) silliness or (in a good sense) trust:--confidence, flank, folly, hope, loin. 
 

See  H3688

title: H3690 · kiclah
text:
feminine of 3689; in a good sense, trust; in a bad one, silliness:--confidence, folly. 
 

See  H3689

title: H3691 · Kiclev
text: probably of foreign origin; Kisleu, the 9th Heb. month:--Chisleu.

title: H3692 · Kiclown
text:
from 3688; hopeful; Kislon, an Israelite:--Chislon. 
 

See  H3688

title: H3693 · K@calown
text:
from 3688; fertile; Kesalon, a place in Palestine:--Chesalon. 
 

See  H3688

title: H3694 · K@cullowth
text:
feminine plural of passive participle of 3688; fattened; Kesulloth, a place in Palestine:--Chesulloth. 
 

See  H3688

title: H3695 · Kacluchiym
text: a plural probably of foreign derivation; Casluchim, a people cognate to the Egyptians:--Casluhim.

title: H3696 · Kicloth Tabor
text:
from the feminine plural of 3689 and 8396; flanks of Tabor; Kisloth-Tabor, a place in Palestine:--Chisloth- tabor. 
 

See  H3689  
See  H8396

title: H3697 · kacam
text:
a primitive root; to shear:--X only, poll.  Compare 3765. 
 

See  H3765

title: H3698 · kuccemeth
text:
from 3697; spelt (from its bristliness as if just shorn):--fitches, rie. 
 

See  H3697

title: H3699 · kacac
text: a primitive root; to estimate:--make count.

title: H3700 · kacaph
text: a primitive root; properly, to become pale, i.e. (by implication) to pine after; also to fear:--(have) desire, be greedy, long, sore.

title: H3701 · keceph
text:
from 3700; silver (from its pale color); by implication, money:--money, price, silver(-ling). 
 

See  H3700

title: H3702 · k@caph (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 3701:--money, silver. 
 

See  H3701

title: H3703 · Kaciphya'
text:
perhaps from 3701; silvery; Casiphja, a place in Bab.:--Casiphia. 
 

See  H3701

title: H3704 · keceth
text:
from 3680; a cushion or pillow (as covering a seat or bed):--pillow. 
 

See  H3680

title: H3705 · k@`an (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) probably from 3652; now:--now. 
 

See  H3652

title: H3706 · k@`eneth (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) or kaeth (Aramaic) {keh-eth'}; feminine of 3705; thus (only in the formula "and so forth"):--at such a time. 
 

See  H3705

title: H3707 · ka`ac
text: a primitive root; to trouble; by implication, to grieve, rage, be indignant:--be angry, be grieved, take indignation, provoke (to anger, unto wrath), have sorrow, vex, be wroth.

title: H3708 · ka`ac
text:
or (in Job) kaoas {kah'-as}; from 3707; vexation:  -anger, angry, grief, indignation, provocation, provoking, X sore, sorrow, spite, wrath. 
 

See  H3707

title: H3709 · kaph
text:
from 3721; the hollow hand or palm (so of the paw of an animal, of the sole, and even of the bowl of a dish or sling, the handle of a bolt, the leaves of a palm-tree); figuratively, power:--branch, + foot, hand((-ful), -dle, (-led)), hollow, middle, palm, paw, power, sole, spoon. 
 

See  H3721

title: H3710 · keph
text:
from 3721; a hollow rock:--rock. 
 

See  H3721

title: H3711 · kaphah
text: a primitive root; properly, to bend, i.e. (figuratively) to tame or subdue:--pacify.

title: H3712 · kippah
text:
feminine of 3709; a leaf of a palm-tree:--branch. 
 

See  H3709

title: H3713 · k@phowr
text:
from 3722; properly, a cover, i.e. (by implication) a tankard (or covered goblet); also white frost (as covering the ground):--bason, hoar(-y) frost. 
 

See  H3722

title: H3714 · kaphiyc
text: from an unused root meaning to connect; a girder:--beam.

title: H3715 · k@phiyr
text:
from 3722; a village (as covered in by walls); also a young lion (perhaps as covered with a mane):--(young) lion, village. Compare 3723. 
 

See  H3722  
See  H3723

title: H3716 · K@phiyrah
text:
feminine of 3715; the village (always with the art.); Kephirah, a place in Palestine:--Chephirah. 
 

See  H3715

title: H3717 · kaphal
text: a primitive root; to fold together; figuratively, to repeat:--double.

title: H3718 · kephel
text:
from 3717; a duplicate:--double. 
 

See  H3717

title: H3719 · kaphan
text: a primitive root; to bend:--bend.

title: H3720 · kaphan
text:
from 3719; hunger (as making to stoop with emptiness and pain):--famine. 
 

See  H3719

title: H3721 · kaphaph
text: a primitive root; to curve:--bow down (self).

title: H3722 · kaphar
text: a primitive root; to cover (specifically with bitumen); figuratively, to expiate or condone, to placate or cancel:-- appease, make (an atonement, cleanse, disannul, forgive, be merciful, pacify, pardon, purge (away), put off, (make) reconcile(-liation).

title: H3723 · kaphar
text:
from 3722; a village (as protected by walls):  -village. Compare 3715. 
 

See  H3722  
See  H3715

title: H3724 · kopher
text:
from 3722; properly, a cover, i.e. (literally) a village (as covered in); (specifically) bitumen (as used for coating), and the henna plant (as used for dyeing); figuratively, a redemption-price:--bribe, camphire, pitch, ransom, satisfaction, sum of money, village. 
 

See  H3722

title: H3725 · kippur
text:
from 3722; expiation (only in plural):  -atonement. 
 

See  H3722

title: H3726 · K@phar ha-`Ammowniy
text:
from 3723 and 5984, with the article interposed; village of the Ammonite; Kefar-ha-Ammoni, a place in Palestine:--Chefar-haamonai. 
 

See  H3723  
See  H5984

title: H3727 · kapporeth
text:
from 3722; a lid (used only of the cover of the sacred Ark):--mercy seat. 
 

See  H3722

title: H3728 · kaphash
text: a primitive root; to tread down; figuratively, to humiliate:--cover.

title: H3729 · k@phath (Aramaic)
text: (Aramaic) a root of uncertain correspondence; to fetter:--bind.

title: H3730 · kaphtor
text: or (Am. 9:1) kaphtowr {kaf-tore'}; probably from an unused root meaning to encircle; a chaplet; but used only in an architectonic sense, i.e. the capital of a column, or a wreath-like button or disk on the candelabrum: knop, (upper) lintel.

title: H3731 · Kaphtor
text:
or (Am. 9:7) Kaphtowr {kaf-tore'}; apparently the same as 3730; Caphtor (i.e. a wreath-shaped island), the original seat of the Philistines:--Caphtor. 
 

See  H3730

title: H3732 · Kaphtoriy
text:
patrial from 3731; a Caphtorite (collectively) or native of Caphtor:--Caphthorim, Caphtorim(-s). 
 

See  H3731

title: H3733 · kar
text:
from 3769 in the sense of plumpness; a ram (as full-grown and fat), including a battering-ram (as butting); hence, a meadow (as for sheep); also a pad or camel's saddle (as puffed out):--captain, furniture, lamb, (large) pasture, ram. See also 1033, 3746. 
 

See  H3769  
See  H1033  
See  H3746

title: H3734 · kor
text:
from the same as 3564; properly, a deep round vessel, i.e. (specifically) a cor or measure for things dry:--cor, measure. Aramaic the same. 
 

See  H3564

title: H3735 · Kara' (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) probably corresponding to 3738 in the sense of piercing (figuratively); to grieve:--be grieved. 
 

See  H3738

title: H3736 · karbel
text:
from the same as 3525; to gird or clothe:  -clothed. 
 

See  H3525

title: H3737 · karb@la` (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) from a verb corresponding to that of 3736; a mantle:--hat. 
 

See  H3736

title: H3738 · karah
text: a primitive root; properly, to dig; figuratively, to plot; generally, to bore or open:--dig, X make (a banquet), open.

title: H3739 · karah
text:
usually assigned as a primitive root, but probably only a special application of 3738 (through the common idea of planning implied in a bargain); to purchase:--buy, prepare. 
 

See  H3738

title: H3740 · kerah
text:
from 3739; a purchase:--provision. 
 

See  H3739

title: H3741 · karah
text:
feminine of 3733; a meadow:--cottage. 
 

See  H3733

title: H3742 · k@ruwb
text: of uncertain derivation; a cherub or imaginary figure:--cherub, (plural) cherubims.

title: H3743 · K@ruwb
text:
the same as 3742; Kerub, a place in Bab.:  -Cherub. 
 

See  H3742

title: H3744 · karowz (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) from 3745; a herald:--herald. 
 

See  H3745

title: H3745 · k@raz (Aramaic)
text: (Aramaic) probably of Greek origin; to proclaim:--make a proclamation.

title: H3746 · kariy

from 3868; perverseness:--perverse. 
 

See  H3868

title: H3892 · lach
text: from an unused root meaning to be new; fresh, i.e. unused or undried:--green, moist.

title: H3893 · leach
text:
from the same as 3892; freshness, i.e. vigor:  -natural force. 
 

See  H3892

title: H3894 · lachuwm
text:
or lachum {law-khoom'}; passive participle of 3898; properly, eaten, i.e. food; also flesh, i.e. body:--while...is eating, flesh. 
 

See  H3898

title: H3895 · l@chiy
text: from an unused root meaning to be soft; the cheek (from its fleshiness); hence, the jaw-bone:--cheek (bone), jaw (bone).

title: H3896 · Lechiy
text:
a form of 3895; Lechi, a place in Palestine:--Lehi. Compare also 7437. 
 

See  H3895  
See  H7437

title: H3897 · lachak
text: a primitive root; to lick:--lick (up).

title: H3898 · lacham
text: a primitive root; to feed on; figuratively, to consume; by implication, to battle (as destruction):--devour, eat, X ever, fight(-ing), overcome, prevail, (make) war(-ring).

title: H3899 · lechem
text:
from 3898; food (for man or beast), especially bread, or grain (for making it):--((shew-))bread, X eat, food, fruit, loaf, meat, victuals. See also 1036. 
 

See  H3898  
See  H1036

title: H3900 · l@chem (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 3899:--feast. 
 

See  H3899

title: H3901 · lachem
text:
from 3898, battle:--war. 
 

See  H3898

title: H3902 · Lachmiy
text:
from 3899; foodful; Lachmi, an Israelite; or rather probably a brief form (or perhaps erroneous transcription) for 1022:-- Lahmi. See also 3433. 
 

See  H3899  
See  H3433  
See  H1022

title: H3903 · Lachmac
text:
probably by erroneous transcription for Lachmam {lakh-mawm'}; from 3899; food-like; Lachmam or Lachmas, a place in Palestine:--Lahmam. 
 

See  H3899

title: H3904 · l@chenah (Aramaic)
text: (Aramaic) from an unused root of uncertain meaning; a concubine:--concubine.

title: H3905 · lachats
text: a primitive root; properly, to press, i.e. (figuratively) to distress:--afflict, crush, force, hold fast, oppress(-or), thrust self.

title: H3906 · lachats
text:
from 3905; distress:--affliction, oppression. 
 

See  H3905

title: H3907 · lachash
text: a primitive root; to whisper; by implication, to mumble a spell (as a magician):--charmer, whisper (together).

title: H3908 · lachash
text:
from 3907; properly, a whisper, i.e. by implication, (in a good sense) a private prayer, (in a bad one) an incantation; concretely, an amulet:--charmed, earring, enchantment, orator, prayer. 
 

See  H3907

title: H3909 · lat
text:
a form of 3814 or else participle from 3874; properly, covered, i.e. secret; by implication, incantation; also secrecy or (adverb) covertly:  -enchantment, privily, secretly, softly. 
 

See  H3814  
See  H3874

title: H3910 · lot
text:
probably from 3874; a gum (from its sticky nature), probably ladanum:--myrrh. 
 

See  H3874

title: H3911 · l@ta'ah
text: from an unused root meaning to hide; a kind of lizard (from its covert habits):--lizard.

title: H3912 · L@tuwshim
text:
masculine plural of passive participle of 3913; hammered (i.e. oppressed) ones; Letushim, an Arabian tribe:--Letushim. 
 

See  H3913

title: H3913 · latash
text: a primitive root; properly, to hammer out (an edge), i.e. to sharpen:--instructer, sharp(-en), whet.

title: H3914 · loyah
text:
a form of 3880; a wreath:--addition. 
 

See  H3880

title: H3915 · layil
text:
or (Isa. 21:11) leyl {lale}; also laylah {lah'- yel-aw}; from the same as 3883; properly, a twist (away of the light), i.e. night; figuratively, adversity:--((mid-))night (season). 
 

See  H3883

title: H3916 · leyl@ya' (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 3815:--night. 
 

See  H3815

title: H3917 · liyliyth
text:
from 3915; a night spectre:--screech owl. 
 

See  H3915

title: H3918 · layish
text:
from 3888 in the sense of crushing; a lion (from his destructive blows):--(old)lion. 
 

See  H3888

title: H3919 · Layish
text:
the same as 3918; Laish, the name of two places in Palestine:--Laish. Compare 3889. 
 

See  H3918  
See  H3889

title: H3920 · lakad
text: a primitive root; to catch (in a net, trap or pit); generally, to capture or occupy; also to choose (by lot); figuratively, to cohere:--X at all, catch (self), be frozen, be holden, stick together, take.

title: H3921 · leked
text:
from 3920; something to capture with, i.e. a noose:--being taken. 
 

See  H3920

title: H3922 · lekah
text:
from 3212; a journey; Lekah, a place in Palestine:  -Lecah. 
 

See  H3212

title: H3923 · Lachiysh
text: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; Lakish, a place in Palestine:--Lachish.

title: H3924 · lula'ah
text:
from the same as 3883; a loop:--loop. 
 

See  H3883

title: H3925 · lamad
text: a primitive root; properly, to goad, i.e. (by implication) to teach (the rod being an Oriental incentive):(un-) accustomed, X diligently, expert, instruct, learn, skilful, teach(-er, - ing).

title: H3926 · l@mow
text: a prol. and separable form of the prepositional prefix; to or for:--at, for, to, upon.

title: H3927 · L@muw'el
text:
or Lmow el {lem-o-ale'}; from 3926 and 410; (belonging) to God; Lemuel or Lemoel, a symbolic name of Solomon:  -Lemuel. 
 

See  H3926  
See  H410

title: H3928 · limmuwd
text:
or limmud {lim-mood'}; from 3925; instructed:  -accustomed, disciple, learned, taught, used. 
 

See  H3925

title: H3929 · Lemek
text: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; Lemek, the name of two antediluvian patriarchs:--Lamech.

title: H3930 · loa`
text:
from 3886; the gullet:--throat. 
 

See  H3886

title: H3931 · la`ab
text: a primitive root; to deride:--mock.

title: H3932 · la`ag
text: a primitive root; to deride; by implication (as if imitating a foreigner) to speak unintelligibly:--have in derision, laugh (to scorn), mock (on), stammering.

title: H3933 · la`ag
text:
from 3932; derision, scoffing:--derision, scorn (-ing). 
 

See  H3932

title: H3934 · la`eg
text:
from 3932; a buffoon; also a foreigner:--mocker, stammering. 
 

See  H3932

title: H3935 · La`dah
text: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; Ladah, an Israelite:--Laadah.

title: H3936 · La`dan
text:
from the same as 3935; Ladan, the name of two Israelites:--Laadan. 
 

See  H3935

title: H3937 · la`az
text: a primitive root; to speak in a foreign tongue:  -strange language.

title: H3938 · la`at
text: a primitive root; to swallow greedily; causatively, to feed:--feed.

title: H3939 · la`anah
text: from an unused root supposed to mean to curse; wormwood (regarded as poisonous, and therefore accursed):--hemlock, wormwood.

title: H3940 · lappiyd
text: or lappid {lap-peed'}; from an unused root probably meaning to shine; a flambeau, lamp or flame:--(fire-)brand, (burning) lamp, lightning, torch.

title: H3941 · Lappiydowth
text:
feminine plural of 3940; Lappidoth, the husband of Deborah:--Lappidoth. 
 

See  H3940

title: H3942 · liphnay
text:
from the prepositional prefix (to or for) and 6440; anterior:--before. 
 

See  H6440

title: H3943 · laphath
text: a primitive root; properly, to bend, i.e. (by implication) to clasp; also (reflexively) to turn around or aside:--take hold, turn aside (self).

title: H3944 · latsown
text:
from 3887; derision:--scornful(-ning). 
 

See  H3887

title: H3945 · latsats
text: a primitive root; to deride:--scorn.

title: H3946 · Laqquwm
text: from an unused root thought to mean to stop up by a barricade; perhaps fortification; Lakkum, a place in Palestine:--Lakum.

title: H3947 · laqach
text: a primitive root; to take (in the widest variety of applications):--accept, bring, buy, carry away, drawn, fetch, get, infold, X many, mingle, place, receive(-ing), reserve, seize, send for, take (away, -ing, up), use, win.

title: H3948 · leqach
text:
from 3947; properly, something received, i.e. (mentally) instruction (whether on the part of the teacher or hearer); also (in an active and sinister sense) inveiglement:--doctrine, learning, fair speech. 
 

See  H3947

title: H3949 · Liqchiy
text:
from 3947; learned; Likchi, an Israelite:--Likhi. 
 

See  H3947

title: H3950 · laqat
text: a primitive root; properly, to pick up, i.e. (generally) to gather; specifically, to glean:--gather (up), glean.

title: H3951 · leqet
text:
from 3950; the gleaning:--gleaning. 
 

See  H3950

title: H3952 · laqaq
text: a primitive root; to lick or lap:--lap, lick.

title: H3953 · laqash
text: a primitive root; to gather the after crop:--gather.

title: H3954 · leqesh
text:
from 3953; the after crop:--latter growth. 
 

See  H3953

title: H3955 · l@shad
text: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; apparently juice, i.e. (figuratively) vigor; also a sweet or fat cake:--fresh, moisture.

title: H3956 · lashown
text:
or lashon {law-shone'}; also (in plural) feminine lshonah {lesh-o-naw'}; from 3960; the tongue (of man or animals), used literally (as the instrument of licking, eating, or speech), and figuratively (speech, an ingot, a fork of flame, a cove of water):--+ babbler,bay, + evil speaker, language, talker, tongue, wedge. 
 

See  H3960

title: H3957 · lishkah
text:
from an unused root of uncertain meaning; a room in a building (whether for storage, eating, or lodging):--chamber, parlour. Compare 5393. 
 

See  H5393

title: H3958 · leshem
text: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; a gem, perhaps the jacinth:--ligure.

title: H3959 · Leshem
text:
the same as 3958; Leshem, a place in Palestine:  -Leshem. 
 

See  H3958

title: H3960 · lashan
text:
a primitive root; properly, to lick; but used only as a denominative from 3956; to wag the tongue, i.e. to calumniate:--accuse, slander. 
 

See  H3956

title: H3961 · lishshan (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 3956; speech, i.e. a nation:--language. 
 

See  H3956

title: H3962 · Lesha`
text: from an unused root thought to mean to break through; a boiling spring; Lesha, a place probably East of the Jordan:--Lasha.

title: H3963 · lethek
text: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; a measure for things dry:--half homer.

title: H3964 · ma' (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 4100; (as indef.) that:--+ what. 
 

See  H4100

title: H3965 · ma`abuwc
text:
from 75; a granary:--storehouse. 
 

See  H75

title: H3966 · m@`od
text:
from the same as 181; properly, vehemence, i.e. (with or without preposition) vehemently; by implication, wholly, speedily, etc. (often with other words as an intensive or superlative; especially when repeated):--diligently, especially, exceeding(-ly), far, fast, good, great(-ly), X  louder and louder, might(-ily, -y), (so) much, quickly, (so) sore, utterly, very (+ much, sore), well. 
 

See  H181

title: H3967 · me'ah
text: or metyah {may-yaw'}; properly, a primitive numeral; a hundred; also as a multiplicative and a fraction:--hundred((-fold), -th), + sixscore.

title: H3968 · Me'ah
text:
the same as 3967; Meah, a tower in Jerusalem:--Meah. 
 

See  H3967

title: H3969 · ma'ah (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 3967:--hundred. 
 

See  H3967

title: H3970 · ma'avay
text:
from 183; a desire:--desire. 
 

See  H183

title: H3971 · m'uwm
text: usually muwm {moom}; as if passive participle from an unused root probably meaning to stain; a blemish (physically or morally):--blemish, blot, spot.

title: H3972 · m@uwmah
text:
apparently a form of 3971; properly, a speck or point, i.e. (by implication) something; with negative, nothing:--fault, + no(-ught), ought, somewhat, any ((no-))thing. 
 

See  H3971

title: H3973 · ma'owc
text:
from 3988; refuse:--refuse. 
 

See  H3988

title: H3974 · ma'owr
text:
or maor {maw-ore'}; also (in plural) feminine mpowrah {meh-o-raw'}; or morah {meh-o-raw'}; from 215; properly, a luminous body  or  luminary,  i.e.  (abstractly) light (as an element): figuratively, brightness, i.e.cheerfulness; specifically, a chandelier:--bright, light. 
 

See  H215

title: H3975 · m@uwrah
text:
feminine passive participle of 215; something lighted, i.e. an aperture; by implication, a crevice or hole (of a serpent):--den. 
 

See  H215

title: H3976 · mo'zen
text:
from 239; (only in the dual) a pair of scales:  -balances. 
 

See  H239

title: H3977 · mo'zen (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 3976:--balances. 
 

See  H3976

title: H3978 · ma'akal
text:
from 398; an eatable (includ. provender, flesh and fruit):--food, fruit, ((bake-)) meat(-s), victual. 
 

See  H398

title: H3979 · ma'akeleth
text:
from 398; something to eat with,- i.e. a knife:--knife. 
 

See  H398

title: H3980 · ma'akoleth
text:
from 398; something eaten (by fire), i.e. fuel:--fuel. 
 

See  H398

title: H3981 · ma'amats
text:
from 553; strength, i.e. (plural) resources:--force. 
 

See  H553

title: H3982 · ma'amar
text:
from 559; something (authoritatively) said, i.e. an edict:--commandment, decree. 
 

See  H559

title: H3983 · me'mar (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 3982:--appointment, word. 
 

See  H3982
